name: Generalized Epilepsy-Paroxysmal Dyskinesia Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Generalized Epilepsy-Paroxysmal Dyskinesia Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of generalized epileptic seizures including tonic-clonic or absence seizures
Episodes of paroxysmal dyskinesia characterized by involuntary, intermittent hyperkinetic movements
Exclusion of other metabolic, structural, or genetic causes of epilepsy and dyskinesia
Positive family history of epilepsy or paroxysmal movement disorders
Improvement of symptoms with antiepileptic or antidyskinetic medications

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both generalized epileptic seizures and paroxysmal dyskinesia episodes with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic causes (e.g., normal serum lactate and ammonia)
imaging: Normal brain MRI or nonspecific mild cortical atrophy
other: EEG showing generalized spike-and-wave discharges during seizures
Video-EEG monitoring capturing dyskinetic episodes without epileptiform activity

distinguishingFeatures: Dyskinesia triggered exclusively by sudden movement
Myoclonic seizures predominant without paroxysmal dyskinesia
Typical EEG with generalized polyspike-and-wave discharges

redFlags: Prolonged status epilepticus requiring intensive care
Failure to respond to standard antiepileptic treatments
references: Orphanet: Generalized Epilepsy-Paroxysmal Dyskinesia Syndrome, ORPHA:79137
Clinical Neurogenetics Journal, 2023; Genetic and Clinical Features of Epilepsy-Dyskinesia Syndromes
Epilepsia, 2022; Diagnostic Criteria and Management of Paroxysmal Dyskinesias
